title: Recursive Self-Editing: LLMs Program Their Own Weight Edits for Self-Improvement
read_level: full (arXiv PDF v1 via pdftotext: Secs 1-6, Tables 1-4, Algorithm 1, Appendices A-B; Figures 1-4 read as text only; no affiliations printed)
metadata_mismatch: none (title, authors, abstract match; metadata abstract uses 'Whenever' where PDF has '; whenever')
why_wsp: Qwen3.8-27B, acting as editor in a sandboxed Python session with a white-box, gradient-free toolkit over its own weights, writes a program that builds a low-rank (LoRA-form) edit to its own weights; the best gate-improving edit is merged and the edited model writes the next edit.
facets: safety (sandboxing, hidden gate, rank/norm caps; no safety evaluation)
editor: the current model M_g itself (Qwen3.8-27B, thinking mode); M_0 is the first editor; no stronger external model
target: its own weights: Qwen3.8-27B (BF16, dense, full-attention + Gated DeltaNet layers); edits are LoRA factors over chosen linear modules, merged as W' = bf16(W + BA)
interface: code/tensor tools (program main(api) composing SVD, activation contrasts, rank-1 projections, singular-value rescaling, LoRA operators, sandboxed CPU PyTorch tensor_compute; no gradient or training tool)
loop: closed-loop with feedback: 5 generations x 8 independent editing sessions (<=30 tool rounds each); each candidate graded once on a hidden 500-problem gate; best strictly positive paired gain merged; later sessions see gate statistics (accuracy, paired gain, CI, fixed/broken ids) but never gate content
self_editing: yes: the editor edits its own weights and the merged model M_{g+1} is the editor of the next generation. Quote: "the merged model Mg+1 is the editor of generation g + 1" (Sec 3.1). 5 generations run; 4 edits accepted (gen 5 delta 0.00, M5 = M4 on gate).
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: Not reported for accepted edits. Caps only: "rank(Bm Am) <= 64, ||Bm Am||F / ||Wg(m)||F <= tau = 0.1" per module (Eq. 1; Table 4). Which modules/layers the accepted edits touched is not reported (Fig. 3 layers are "examples").

headline_results.quote: SELFWRITE raises gate accuracy from 73.95% for M0 to 76.45% for the final model M5, a cumulative gain of 2.50 points.
The accepted edits gain +1.20, +0.50, +0.10 and +0.70 points.

headline_results.claim: Held-out test avg@4 (M0 vs M5 only)
headline_results.quote: avg@4 accuracy rises from 76.30% for M0 to 77.75% for M5 (+1.45 points)
pass@4 from 82.60% to 84.80% (+2.20 points; Table 2) without a single gradient step
the fourth generation, written by M3, brings the second-largest step: the edited model remains an effective editor of its own weights.

cost.quote: per generation, shared by the 8 sessions: 7,200 s for programs, 600 s for exploration
30 tool rounds, 100 tool calls, 160,000 completion tokens, 2,400 s per candidate
8 per run: 7 vLLM replicas of Mg (editor, scoring, LoRA hot-loading) + 1 tool GPU

cost.claim: Cost driver (qualitative; total wall-clock/tokens not reported)
cost.quote: The cost of a generation is dominated by sampling the screen and grading eight candidates

baselines_and_controls: No external baselines or ablations: no comparison to gradient fine-tuning/LoRA training, SEAL-style self-training, an external (non-self) editor, random or untargeted low-rank edits of equal norm, best-of-8 selection of random edits, or prompting. Only reference is the unedited M0. Controls are protocol-level: disjoint gate/test/screen splits, decontamination, test split "never screened, gated or shown to the editor" (Sec 5.2), deterministic grading, fixed seed.
runs_and_variance: Single run of 5 generations; no repeated runs or seeds. Scoring is 4 samples per problem with fixed seed 42. A 95% paired-bootstrap CI is computed for each candidate's gate gain and fed to later editors, but CIs are not reported in Table 2; no CI or significance for the test gains. Test accuracy reported only for M0 and M5.
robustness_of_edits: not tested (no fine-tuning, quantization or other-domain evaluation; only held-out split from same DAPO-Math pool)
verification: none formal; acceptance by deterministic answer-matching on a hidden 500-problem gate (paired gain > 0, max over 8 candidates); edits checked against rank/norm caps
memorization_vs_reasoning: n/a (no analysis of what the accepted edits do or why they help; the activation-contrast + project_out recipe is "suggested in the editor's prompt" (Sec 3.3))
limitations_stated: No limitations section. Future work lists: "self-editing across several domains at once, longer horizons with more generations, larger editors, and richer edit spaces beyond low-rank updates" (Sec 6).
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al., Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (blog, 2026)
2611.09376 Can LLMs Debug Robots by Editing Their Weights?
notes_for_survey: Direct B6 instance: same model is editor and target, and the edited model writes subsequent edits (4 accepted edits in 5 generations, ~+2.5 gate / +1.45 test avg@4 points on DAPO-Math). Edits are selected as the max of 8 candidates on the same gate whose accuracy is reported, so gate gains include selection; the held-out test gain is the cleaner number but has no CI, single run, and no random-edit, external-editor or gradient fine-tune baseline. What the accepted edits changed (modules, rank, norm) is not reported.
